page: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores mapped to an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.4 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c5.2xlarge in the average performance tier for most standard compute workloads. The instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1175.0 and a multi-core score of 4531.0. Its Intel Xeon architecture supports AVX and AVX-512 instructions, which assist in vector processing tasks, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 8888.09 and a ray tracing score of 5914.0. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and image processing benchmarks fall into the weak category, indicating potential bottlenecks during highly parallelized decompression or media-heavy tasks.

The DDR4 memory subsystem delivers a read-only cached bandwidth of 437.77 GB/sec, which drops to 50.41 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database and key-value store simulations, the instance processed 7.77 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a static web serving throughput of 7.26 GB/sec. For machine learning, the lack of a GPU limits its utility; LLM inference on a medium 7B model is poor, with prompt processing speeds of 11.09 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c5.2xlarge offers a dedicated compute profile without the overhead of bundled local storage, making it a resource-dense option for compute-bound workloads that rely on network-attached storage. It is best suited for batch processing, web serving, distributed analytics, and moderate compilation tasks, rather than memory-intensive databases or large-scale AI inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor running at 3.4 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores) and 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying instead on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4531.0 and a static web serving throughput of 7.26 GB/sec. While it supports AVX-512 vector instructions, multi-threaded decompression and LLM inference tasks show weaker performance. This instance is qualitatively cost-effective for compute-heavy, network-storage-reliant workloads such as batch processing, web serving, and software compilation.
